We have applied first template 324324, got precursors: product1: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1" and "Nc1ccccc1N". That seems plausible: the amide N attached to phenyl? Actually original had ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (an anilide with an aniline). The first step likely disconnection of the amide to give carboxylic acid and aniline with amine? The template gave product1 (the rest) and aniline with two amines? Actually "Nc1ccccc1N" is p-phenylenediamine? Wait SMILES: N c1 c c c c c1 N => aniline with two amine groups? That's p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene). Good.

Second template 1914396 applied to the first precursor (the sulfonyl phenyl with a side chain containing C=O O). It gave two precursors: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1" and "O=C(O)CC(=O)O". So we have broken the double bond and carboxylic acid? Actually we got a benzoic acid side chain? The second precursor is a dicarboxylic acid (oxalic acid? Actually O=C(O)CC(=O)O is succinic acid). So we have a succinic acid as a building block.

Now we need third template 733 applied to something to get final precursors. Likely apply to the remaining intermediate "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1". Template 733 maybe does a sulfonylation? Not sure. Let's check if template 733 matches that intermediate.
